text.p: Transport and logistics supplier Schenker-Rhenus AG said its business had grown strongly in the first five months of 1997 as the company benefited from a cost-cutting restructuring.

Company chairman Bernd Malmstroem said the international management of the three business divisions -- air and seafreight forwarder Schenker International AG, groupage division Schenker Eurocargo AG and logistics company Rhenus AG -- was being centralised at the Schenker-Rhenus head office in Essen.
This included the transfer of the Schenker International AG office, headed by Klaus Geissler, from the Frankfurt cargo village in Keisterbach.
"If we want to be one company then all the suppliers must be in one location where all can co-operate and decide more quickly," he said at the Transport 97 trade fair in Munich.

"We will build up the three areas and that means we cannot work at three different locations. We have cut overlaps and have just one controlling department for the three areas and that leads to clear cost advantages," he added.

But the three companies will remain separate profit centres, with their own local operational management teams, while Schenker-Rhenus will be responsible for group strategy and providing multimodal logistics solutions.
Malmstroem said the Schenker-Rhenus group was currently in a consolidation phase after sales fell last year.

"The first five months of the year show an upward trend in all areas, which is very satisfactory," he said. But he declined to give any precise business development figures apart from noting that freight volumes were rising faster than sales revenue,
In 1996, total Schenker-Rhenus group turnover fell 1.2 percent to 6.45 billion marks, excluding inter-company sales, according to the annual report of parent company Stinnes AG.

Schenker International saw sales rise 1.2 percent to 2.5 billion marks in 1996 but Schenker Eurocargo sales fell 2.2 percent to 2.47 billion marks and Rhenus sales fell 7.6 percent to 1.2 billion marks.
Schenker International managing director Guenter Mueller said inner-Asia traffic was showing double-figure growth and noted that investment in the Sword communications network would be increased.

Schenker Eurocargo managing director Gerhard Monning said the overland transport division had increased productivity and was now making money, although freight prices remained low and were under pressure.

"Price increases would certainly be necessary but we have a market over-capacity and that makes increases difficult to put through. I canot see a general rate increase in the next few years," he said.
But he added: "There are some areas where prices must go up because the rates are not enough to cover costs."
